title: feat(perf): system prompt override for multi-turn benchmarks
body:
## User problem

Simulating a production Agent under `evalscope perf --multi-turn` is currently impossible without hand-rolled scripts: open models don't emit the 4000-token tool-call system prompt a real deployment uses, `custom_multi_turn` reuses the dataset's own prompts, and `swe_smith` can't take a custom system prompt at all. Users lose EvalScope's RPS / P99 / TTFT / TPOT / KV-cache metrics the moment they step outside the tool.

This completes the remaining ask in #1358 (per-turn `max_tokens` landed in #1767): a CLI system-prompt override for multi-turn benchmarks.

## UX decision

`--multi-turn-system-prompt "..."` applies once per conversation (turn 0), to warmup and measured conversations alike:

- dataset's first message is `system` → its content is **replaced** (explicit user intent wins);
- otherwise → the override is **inserted first**;
- flag omitted → dataset prompts untouched.

```bash
evalscope perf \
  --model qwen-plus --api openai --dataset share_gpt_zh_multi_turn \
  --multi-turn --max-turns 10 \
  --multi-turn-system-prompt "You are a tool-calling agent. ..." \
  --multi-turn-per-turn-tokens "[150, 150, 150, 150, 150, 150, 150, 150, 150, 1000]"
```

## Changes

- `Arguments.multi_turn_system_prompt` + CLI `--multi-turn-system-prompt`
- `apply_system_prompt_override()` in `MultiTurnStrategy` module; hooked on turn 0. It only touches the per-conversation `context` (fresh list of copied messages), never shared dataset state.
- 6 unit tests (replace / insert / empty / no-op / Arguments parsing / default), no network needed.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/perf/test_perf_multi_turn.py::TestMultiTurnSystemPromptOverride` — 6 passed
- CLI → `Arguments.from_args` round-trip verified
- `ruff check` — all checks passed

Part of #1358 (completes it together with #1767)

title: fix(alpaca_eval): count a win as 1 and a loss as 0
body:
Fixes #1770

Since #1601, AlpacaEval counts a win as 0.75 and a loss as 0.25. The reported win rate is therefore 0.25 + 0.5 * p, where p is the true win rate. For example, 8 wins out of 10 show up as 0.65.

The reduce step builds PairwisePlacementOutcome and PairwiseOutcome without a strength value, so both use the default "weak". Arena-Hard and GeneralArena read the strength from labels such as A>>B and A>B. The AlpacaEval judge only answers m or M, so it has no slight preference to express.

What I changed:

1. The reduce step in alpaca_eval_adapter.py now marks every outcome as strong. A win scores 1 and a loss scores 0. A split verdict under position swap still scores 0.5.
2. The AlpacaEval evaluation_version goes from v1.0 to v1.1. AGENTS.md asks for a minor bump when a change affects the default scores, and the bump keeps old cached scores apart from new ones.
3. The position swap test now expects 1.0 when the candidate wins both placements. It expected 0.75 before, and that value was the bug.
4. A new test covers the default single pass. A win gives 1.0 and a loss gives 0.0.

I did not change PairwiseOutcome.score. The weak and strong scale is right for Arena-Hard and GeneralArena, so the fix belongs in the AlpacaEval adapter. It also matches the code before #1601, where the adapter returned 1 for M and 0 otherwise.

Tests:

- pytest tests/api/judge: 129 passed. The three AlpacaEval cases fail on main.
- pytest tests/api/test_benchmark_registry_contract.py: 27 passed.
- pre-commit on the changed files: all hooks pass.

title: fix(hallusion_bench): align fAcc/qAcc grouping with official evaluation
body:
## Problem

`HallusionBenchAdapter.aggregate_scores` computes figure-level (`fAcc`) and question-pair (`qAcc`) accuracy differently from the official HallusionBench evaluation, corrupting both metrics on the default `HallusionBench` dataset.

**1. The grouping key drops `category`.** The current key is:

```python
key = f'{subcategory}_{set_id}_{group_id}'   # group_id = figure_id or question_id
```

HallusionBench has two categories, `VD` and `VS`, and they **reuse the same** `subcategory` / `set_id` / `figure_id` / `question_id` numbering. Omitting `category` merges distinct figures/questions from different categories into a single group. On the official data (1129 records) this collapses **27 figure keys** and **26 question keys** across `VD`/`VS` (e.g. `ocr_0_0` and `chart_0_1` exist under both categories).

**2. `fAcc` counts VS "no-figure" records.** VS entries with `figure_id == 0` are text-only (no supplementary figure). The official eval excludes them from figure-level accuracy. The default data contains **178** such records, all currently counted as spurious figure groups.

## Reference

Both behaviours come straight from the official implementation — [`tianyi-lab/HallusionBench` `utils.py`](https://github.com/tianyi-lab/HallusionBench/blob/main/utils.py):

- `get_eval_fig` (fAcc): key = `"_".join([category, subcategory, set_id, figure_id])`, and it skips records where `category == "VS" and figure_id == "0"`.
- `get_eval_pair_all` (qAcc): key = `"_".join([category, subcategory, set_id, question_id])`.

## Fix

Include `category` in the grouping key, and skip VS `figure_id == 0` records for figure-level accuracy. Question- and answer-level accuracy still see every record.

## Verification

Added `tests/benchmark/test_hallusion_bench.py`, which fails before this change and passes after:

- `test_grouping_key_separates_categories`: two rows sharing `chart_0_1` under `VD` vs `VS` (both `figure_id == 1`, isolating the category effect). Before: one merged group → `fAcc`/`qAcc = 0.0`. After: two groups, one correct → `0.5`.
- `test_figure_accuracy_skips_vs_no_figure_records`: a VS `figure_id == 0` record is dropped from `fAcc` but still counts toward `aAcc`/`qAcc`.

Local run: `tests/benchmark/test_hallusion_bench.py` + `tests/metrics` + `tests/report/semantics/test_complex_aggregations.py` → 97 passed. `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on the changed adapter.

title: feat(perf): per-turn max_tokens override for multi-turn benchmarks
body:
## Summary

Multi-turn perf benchmarks (`--multi-turn`) currently have no way to set per-turn `max_tokens` from the CLI. The global `--max-tokens` applies uniformly to every turn, but real-world agent workloads often need different output caps per turn (e.g. 150 tokens for tool-call turns, 1000 for the final answer).

This PR adds `--multi-turn-per-turn-tokens` to fill that gap.

## Changes

- `Arguments.multi_turn_per_turn_tokens`: `List[Optional[int]]` field with JSON validator
- CLI `--multi-turn-per-turn-tokens "[150, 150, 1000]"` argument
- `MultiTurnStrategy._worker`: applies CLI override by turn index (highest priority), falling back to `Turn.max_tokens` (trace replay) then global `--max-tokens`
- 6 new unit tests covering parsing, validation, and fallback behavior

## Usage

```bash
evalscope perf \
  --model qwen-plus \
  --api openai \
  --dataset random_multi_turn \
  --multi-turn \
  --max-turns 10 \
  --multi-turn-per-turn-tokens "[150, 150, 150, 150, 150, 150, 150, 150, 150, 1000]"
```

## Verification

- `pytest tests/perf/test_perf_multi_turn.py::TestMultiTurnPerTurnTokens` — 6 passed
- `ruff check` — all checks passed

Fixes #1358

title: fix(agent): prevent zero answers from falling back to assistant text
body:
## Summary

In an agent evaluation, a benchmark sample may have `0` as its expected answer. When a provider returns that answer as a JSON number through the `submit` tool, EvalScope previously treated it as missing because numeric zero is falsy in Python.

For example, with assistant content `"I am confident"` and submit answer `0`, the final prediction could become `"I am confident"` instead of the expected `"0"`. This can incorrectly score otherwise valid zero-answer samples.

This change preserves an explicitly submitted `0` as `"0"`. Fallback to assistant content now happens only when the answer is missing, null, or empty. The fix applies to the shared ReAct and Function Calling strategies.

## Tests

- Added three regression tests for numeric-zero submit answers
- 116 relevant agent tests passed
- Ruff check and format check passed

One unrelated SWE-bench test was excluded because its optional dependency is unavailable; the same failure occurs on the unchanged main branch.

title: fix(eval): correct judge rendering, metric scoring, and bootstrap RNG
body:
Fixes #1697.

This fixes four scoring correctness issues: model text can expand judge-template placeholders, arena confidence intervals depend on unrelated global RNG activity, metric exceptions count as successful zero scores, and inclusion accuracy uses different matching rules for strings and lists.

- Render judge placeholders in one pass over the original template. Inserted questions, predictions, and references remain literal, including `{gold}`, JSON, and backslashes.
- Give `general_arena` bootstrap its own RNG, seeded from `TaskConfig.seed`. Fixed seeds reproduce confidence intervals regardless of global RNG consumption; explicit `None` retains nondeterministic sampling without modifying global RNG state.
- Omit failed metric keys and mark fully failed samples `EXCLUDED` or partially failed samples `DEGRADED`. Preserve valid metrics and their denominators through judge fallback and LLM recall, including a missing primary metric and equivalent metric names. When the judge recovers a completely failed rule, align equivalent metric names with the rule declaration so `acc` and `accuracy` do not split the cross-sample aggregation denominator.
- Match one complete, normalized acceptable answer for `allow_inclusion`. Lists remain alternatives (including MMLU-Redux single-choice answers); string references become a single alternative, so `York` no longer matches `New York`. Case and surrounding whitespace follow the existing normalization rules, and blank predictions do not receive credit.

The bootstrap issue is global-RNG coupling, not an absence of seeding in the standard entry point: `run_task` already defaults to seed 42. This does not change `arena_hard`, whose current aggregation does not call bootstrap. The AIME/AIR-Bench parsing defects in #1578 were already fixed by #1588 and subsequently migrated to JSON contracts in #1601; those adapters are unchanged here.

### Compatibility

`general_arena`, `mmlu_redux`, and `trivia_qa` move to evaluation version `v1.1`. A shared scoring version is also included in native cache fingerprints so old scores cannot bypass the common judge and metric fixes. This invalidates existing native score-cache identities, including benchmarks outside these three: use `rerun_review=True` to reuse predictions and recompute reviews. Legacy fingerprints remain calculated with their original algorithm for provenance tracking.

### Validation

Four of the 10 new cross-sample aggregation cases fail against `e0400d03`: equivalent judge and rule names produce duplicate accuracy aggregates with one sample each instead of one aggregate with two samples.

The results below are from the current revision unless marked as earlier. Regression tests were run against the old behavior and rerun after each fix. All judge responses use offline doubles.

- Python 3.13: **281 passed** across judge contracts/execution, adapter scoring, evaluation versioning, metrics/aggregators, and arena bootstrap:
  ```sh
  python -m pytest tests/api/judge tests/api/test_metric_failure_status.py tests/api/test_default_data_adapter.py tests/api/test_scoring_policy.py tests/api/test_evaluation_versioning.py tests/metrics tests/benchmark/test_arena_bootstrap.py -q --tb=short
  ```
- Earlier Python 3.12 focused regressions: **64 passed, 3 skipped**; the three real-ELO adapter cases were skipped because scikit-learn is unavailable in that environment, and passed under Python 3.13.
- `python -m pytest tests/cli/test_all.py::TestRun::test_ci_lite -v -s -p no:warnings`: **1 passed**, using the mock model.
- `make lint`: **passed**.

title: fix(mcp): preserve initialization errors and support service stdio
body:
MCP HTTP initialization failures currently surface as `concurrent.futures.CancelledError`, hiding the underlying connection or HTTP error. Handle cancellation during initialization and unwind the async exit stack in the owning task, preserving the original exception and releasing transport resources.

Service workers also capture stderr with `StringIO`, which prevents lazily imported MCP stdio clients from starting subprocesses (`UnsupportedOperation: fileno`). Capture stderr in a temporary text file with a real file descriptor while retaining diagnostics in task errors.

Fixes #1693.

Validation:
- Regression tests fail before the fix and pass afterward, covering connection failures, HTTP 401/500, external cancellation, repeated stdio MCP sessions in spawned workers, and stderr forwarding.
- 60 related agent/service tests passed with MCP 1.29.1; CI smoke test and `make lint` passed.
- Actual `POST /api/v1/eval/invoke` checks with `mock_llm`, a local single-sample dataset, and MCP 1.29.0: stdio and healthy HTTP complete successfully; failed HTTP connections retain `httpx.ConnectError` in the error response.

Healthy HTTP transport worked before the fix as well; this change corrects failure reporting and cleanup rather than claiming every HTTP endpoint was broken.

title: fix(perf): measure TTFT from reasoning output
body:
## Summary

Fix streamed-output timing in the `evalscope perf` OpenAI-compatible API path for multiple reasoning representations. Live endpoint validation has now been completed on both GLM and Kimi series models.

- Recognize `delta.content` and `delta.reasoning_content`, falling back to `delta.reasoning` when `reasoning_content` is not a non-empty string.
- Recognize displayable `delta.reasoning_details[*].text/summary` as output for TTFT and inter-chunk latency (ITL).
- Keep structured reasoning out of `generated_text`, since providers may return incremental or cumulative values.
- Continue ignoring role-only, usage-only, type-only, and encrypted-data-only chunks when measuring output timing.
- Add deterministic regression coverage for scalar reasoning aliases and structured reasoning streams.

## Root cause and relationship to #1463

This complements #1463, which fixed the same class of reasoning-field compatibility issue in the synchronous and asynchronous model stream collectors in `evalscope/models/utils/openai.py`.

Performance benchmarking uses a separate SSE processing path in `evalscope/perf/plugin/api/default_api.py`. The metadata-chunk fix in v1.11.1 only treated `content` and `reasoning_content` as output there. Servers returning `delta.reasoning` or displayable structured reasoning could therefore leave `first_chunk_latency` at its default `0.0` during reasoning-only output, distorting TTFT percentiles and derived decoding metrics.

This PR closes that remaining gap in the performance path and extends timing recognition to the structured text/summary representation. It does not change the TPOT formula or percentile calculation.

## Verification

### Live GLM and Kimi endpoint tests

Both series were tested with streaming requests, 8 measured requests per run, concurrency 4, `max_tokens=16`, `temperature=0`, and random prompts configured at 128 tokens using the same local tokenizer. The Kimi run used the `public/kimi-k3` model profile. These short runs validate reasoning-only stream timing rather than model throughput or answer quality.

| Tested model | Before: successful requests | Before: TTFT | After: successful requests | After: TTFT range | After: average TTFT |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GLM-series deployment | 8/8 | 0.0 ms for all requests | 8/8 | 911.78–1609.51 ms | 1286.49 ms |
| Kimi series (`public/kimi-k3`) | 8/8 | 0.0 ms for all requests | 8/8 | 434.12–1062.84 ms | 776.05 ms |

- Saved response streams for both tested endpoints contain non-empty `delta.reasoning` output, directly exercising the alias handling.
- After the fix, every measured request has positive TTFT within its total latency, and both runs produce monotonic, non-zero TTFT percentiles.
- Kimi's corrected TTFT percentiles are p50 = 740.84 ms, p95 = 1062.84 ms, and p99 = 1062.84 ms; average ITL is 24.17 ms.
- The Kimi before/after comparison and the 31-test regression suite were run against PR head `3ee6b6d2` and the unpatched baseline as applicable. The earlier GLM results were rechecked against their saved per-request database and reports.
- Structured `reasoning_details` handling is covered by deterministic regression tests; the live GLM and Kimi streams above validate `delta.reasoning`.

### Automated checks

- `pytest tests/perf/test_perf_streaming.py::TestDefaultApiPluginMetrics tests/perf/test_stream_metrics.py tests/perf/test_percentile_metrics.py -q` — 31 passed, rerun on the current PR revision.
- `make lint` — passed during initial PR validation.
- `pytest tests/cli/test_all.py::TestRun::test_ci_lite -v -s -p no:warnings` — passed during initial PR validation.

Fixes #1694
Related to #1463

title: fix(tools): preserve literal values in JSON schemas
body:
JSON schema type normalization currently descends into every dictionary and list, including literal values in `default` and `enum`. For example, a Pydantic tool parameter default of `{"type": "str"}` is advertised to the model as `{"type": "string"}`.

Normalize only the current schema node. Pydantic already validates nested `properties`, `items`, `additionalProperties`, and `anyOf` entries as `JSONSchema` instances, so nested type aliases continue to work while literal values remain intact.

The regression tests cover defaults, enum values, all supported nested schema fields, unchanged input data, and a Pydantic tool parameter. All seven new cases fail against the unmodified base.

Validation (Python 3.12):

- `pytest tests/utils/test_json_schema.py tests/agent/test_tool_argument_validation.py`: **24 passed, 6 subtests passed**.
- `pytest tests/cli/test_all.py::TestRun::test_ci_lite -v -s -p no:warnings`: passed using `mock_llm`.
- `make lint` and `make lint-imports`: passed.

title: fix(models): preserve Anthropic image URL sources
body:
HTTP(S) images passed to the Anthropic backend are currently serialized as `source.type="base64"`, with the URL itself in `source.data`. Emit Anthropic URL image sources for these inputs, and keep local files and data URIs as base64 sources. Cache-control metadata remains attached to the image block.

The new message-conversion tests cover HTTP, HTTPS, local files, data URIs, and cache-control preservation. Against the unmodified base, both URL cases fail and both base64 cases pass.

Validation (Python 3.12, Anthropic SDK installed):

- Anthropic image, prompt-cache, tool-ID, stream-retry, client-error and async-client tests: **60 passed**.
- `pytest tests/cli/test_all.py::TestRun::test_ci_lite -v -s -p no:warnings`: passed using `mock_llm`.
- `make lint` and `make lint-imports`: passed.
- The full `tests/models` collection requires optional `torch`, which is absent in this environment; the unmodified base has the same two collection errors. No live Anthropic request was made.

title: fix(perf): include response body time in embedding and rerank latency
body:
Embedding and rerank benchmarks currently stop their timers as soon as HTTP response headers arrive. Reading the JSON or text body happens afterward, so response transfer time is omitted from request latency and the metrics wall-time window. This can understate latency and inflate QPS, especially for large embedding responses.

Move the existing completion timestamp and latency assignments after the response body has been consumed, for both successful and HTTP error responses. Body-read exceptions still follow the existing failure handling: the plugin marks the request failed, and `AioHttpClient.post` fills in an incomplete failure timestamp. This change does not introduce a new exception-timing policy.

Validation uses a local aiohttp HTTP server that flushes headers, delays the body, and records when the body is sent. All eight cases fail on the unmodified base because the recorded completion time precedes the body; they pass after the fix. The cases cover embedding/rerank, HTTP 200/500, JSON/text fallback, and the metrics accumulator's wall-time window.

Validation:
- Targeted latency and adjacent metrics regression tests: 61 passed on Python 3.12.13 and Python 3.13.13.
- `make lint`: passed, including the new test.
- CI lite smoke: 1 passed with the mock model; the API-key-gated perf sweep was skipped.
- `make lint-imports`: 5 contracts kept, 0 broken.

No external embedding/rerank model service was used.

title: fix(ifbench): guard StopWordPercentageChecker against word-less responses
body:
### Problem

`StopWordPercentageChecker.check_following` (instruction `ratio:stop_words`) divides by the word count without guarding it:

```python
num_words = instructions_util.count_words(value)
num_stopwords = instructions_util.count_stopwords(value)
stopword_percentage = (num_stopwords / num_words) * 100
```

`count_words` uses a `\w+` tokenizer, so any response that contains **no word tokens** — only punctuation, symbols, emoji or whitespace (`"..."`, `"---"`, `"***"`, `"😀"`) — makes `num_words == 0` and raises `ZeroDivisionError`.

This is reachable on real, default runs:

- In both `test_instruction_following_strict` and `test_instruction_following_loose`, the response is only guarded by `response.strip()`. A non-empty but word-less response (e.g. a model that emits only punctuation/emoji) passes that guard and hits the division.
- The loose path additionally evaluates markdown-stripped (`response.replace('*', '')`) and first/last-line-removed variants, so even a normally-formatted response can reduce to a word-less variant and trigger the crash.
- The exception is swallowed in `IFBenchAdapter.match_score`, which sets `score.value = {}`. That discards the results of **every other instruction on that prompt**, not just this checker, and corrupts the aggregate metric.

### Reproduction

```python
from evalscope.benchmarks.ifbench import instructions

c = instructions.StopWordPercentageChecker('ratio:stop_words')
c.build_description(percentage=50)
c.check_following('...')   # ZeroDivisionError: division by zero
c.check_following('😀😀')  # ZeroDivisionError: division by zero
```

### Fix

Restore the guard that upstream [IFBench](https://github.com/allenai/IFBench) has and that evalscope dropped — return `False` when there are no words:

```python
num_words = instructions_util.count_words(value)
if num_words == 0:
    return False
```

This matches upstream verifier behavior exactly and keeps the scoring for the rest of the prompt intact.

### Verification

- Added parametrized regression tests for punctuation/symbol/emoji/whitespace-only responses, plus a normal-response case. Confirmed they raise `ZeroDivisionError` before the fix and pass after it.
- `pytest tests/benchmark/test_ifbench_instructions.py` — 28 passed.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on the changed files.

Not bumping `evaluation_version`: no previously *valid* score changes — word-less responses always errored out (never produced a score), so this only replaces a crash with the upstream-defined `False`, consistent with #1756 which aligned verifiers without a bump.

May be related to #1606 (ifbench metric errors on native runs); leaving it open rather than auto-closing since I can't confirm the reported error is this exact crash.

title: fix(benchmarks): match archive members exactly in mvbench/videomme_v2 video lookup
body:
## Summary

Harden MVBench archive-member lookup with exact relative-path matching (with a basename fallback), aligned with tvbench, so a requested video resolves to the correct member instead of a substring-suffix collision.

## Scope

MVBench only. The Video-MME-v2 change has been dropped: its IDs are pinned to three fixed-length digits (`001`–`800`) and the `NNN.zip` archives only contain three-digit names, so `expected` can never be a proper suffix of another member — that half was purely defensive.

## Real collision (default `action_antonym` subset)

Contrary to my earlier note, the public MVBench mirror **does** reproduce a collision on the default run path. `DEFAULT_SUBSET_LIST = ['action_antonym']` pulls from `ssv2_video.zip`, whose members are Something-Something-v2 ids — non-zero-padded, variable-length numbers. The archive contains both `ssv2_video/9741.mp4` and `ssv2_video/209741.mp4`.

- Annotation requests `9741.mp4`.
- Old lookup: `name.endswith("9741.mp4")` matches both members, and `sorted(matches)[0]` returns `ssv2_video/209741.mp4` (lexically `'2' < '9'`).
- The wrong video is silently fed to the model; the item is scored incorrectly with no error raised.

The patched lookup resolves `9741.mp4` to `ssv2_video/9741.mp4`. Independently verified in the ModelScope mirror by @Yunnglin.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/benchmark/test_archive_member_lookup.py` (4 passed)
- Regression test uses the real names: `9741.mp4` must resolve to `ssv2_video/9741.mp4` when `209741.mp4` is also present. It fails against the pre-fix lookup and passes after.

title: fix(perf): keep a rerank request successful when the top score is not a number
body:
## Problem

`OpenaiRerankPlugin.process_request` (`evalscope/perf/plugin/api/openai_rerank_api.py`, used by `evalscope perf --api openai_rerank` / `--api rerank`) summarises a successful response with

```python
score = top_result.get('relevance_score', top_result.get('score', 0))
output.generated_text = f'top_score={score:.4f}, num_results={len(results)}'
```

`dict.get()` only substitutes the default when the key is *absent*. If the server returns the key with `null` (or a stringified number) the f-string raises, and because it runs inside the same `try` whose handler sets `output.success = False`, a genuine HTTP 200 with valid results is recorded as a failed benchmark request. Reproduced against a real local `aiohttp.web` server through the unmodified module:

```
case=null_relevance_score  server answered 200 with results: True   output.success = False
                           output.error = TypeError: unsupported format string passed to NoneType.__format__
case=null_score_key        output.success = False
case=string_score          output.success = False  (ValueError: Unknown format code 'f' for object of type 'str')
case=normal                output.success = True   generated_text='top_score=0.8421, num_results=2'
```

Downstream, `benchmark_util.py` only accumulates `n_success`, latency and token samples when `data.success` is true, so such requests are dropped from the statistics and pull the success rate down (`summary.py` warns below 95 %). The plugin's own `parse_responses()` degrades gracefully on malformed payloads instead of failing the request; this cosmetic summary line is the only place where a payload detail decides success.

Reachability, honestly: the default perf path reaches this as soon as a server puts `null` or a string in the top result's score. I did not find a specific production rerank server that does so (the documented targets declare the score as a float), so this is a robustness fix for non-conforming servers rather than a reproducible failure with a known backend.

## Change

Format the score with `.4f` when it is an `int`/`float`, otherwise fall back to `str(score)` (so a `null` shows as `top_score=None` rather than being disguised as `0.0000`). Nothing else in the request path changes; 18 numeric inputs (ints, floats, bools, ±inf, nan, huge ints) produce byte-identical summaries before and after.

## Tests

`tests/perf/test_rerank_process_request.py` (`IsolatedAsyncioTestCase` + mocked session, same style as `test_perf_streaming.py`): numeric score, `score`-key fallback, `null` score, string score. On `main`: 2 failed (the `null` and string cases, `False is not true` with the `TypeError`/`ValueError` in the log); with this change: 4 passed. The other offline perf tests (`test_openai_api_parse_responses`, metrics/percentile/stream/trace, arguments, request build errors) still pass. `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean.

title: fix: give logger calls a placeholder for their extra positional arguments
body:
## What

Five `logger.*` calls pass a value as an extra positional argument without a `%`-placeholder in the message:

| file | call |
|---|---|
| `evalscope/backend/rag_eval/clip_benchmark/utils/webdataset_convert.py` (×2) | `logger.info('Final dataset size:', nsamples)` |
| `evalscope/benchmarks/docmath/utils.py` | `logger.error('Error: ', prediction, type(prediction))` |
| `evalscope/benchmarks/image_edit/gedit/utils.py` | `logger.info('Now fixing: ', json_str)` |
| `evalscope/benchmarks/image_edit/gedit/utils.py` | `logger.info('Error: Cannot fix', json_str)` |

`evalscope.utils.logger.get_logger()` returns a standard `logging.Logger`, so the record is formatted with `msg % args`; with no placeholder that raises `TypeError: not all arguments converted during string formatting`. `logging` catches it, prints `--- Logging error ---` plus a traceback to stderr, and the message itself is never emitted:

```python
>>> log.info('Final dataset size:', 5)
--- Logging error ---
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
TypeError: not all arguments converted during string formatting
Call stack: ...
Message: 'Final dataset size:'
Arguments: (5,)
```

The docmath and gedit sites are on error-handling paths (`except` blocks), so the diagnostics meant to explain a failure were the ones being lost.

## Change

Add the missing `%s` placeholders. No behaviour change beyond the messages now actually being logged.

## Checks

- No test added: the fix is five format strings; the failure mode above is standard `logging` behaviour.

title: fix(agent): remove the temporary HOME after codex/hermes/gemini-cli runs
body:
## What

`CodexRunner`, `HermesRunner` and `GeminiCliRunner` call `_resolve_home()` on every `run()`, which returns `tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='evalscope-<runner>-')` whenever no `home_override` is configured. The directory is handed to the CLI as `HOME` / `HERMES_HOME` and then forgotten — nothing removes it, so every evaluated sample leaves an `evalscope-codex-*` / `evalscope-hermes-*` / `evalscope-gemini-cli-*` directory behind (with whatever the CLI wrote into it: skills, config, caches).

The other three runners already handle this: `ClaudeCodeRunner`, `OpenCodeRunner` and `DeepSeekHarnessRunner` compute `owns_home_dir = home_dir is not None and self._home_override is None` and `shutil.rmtree(home_dir, ignore_errors=True)` in a `finally`. This PR applies the same pattern to the remaining three, so all six runners behave the same.

- `home_override=<path>` (user-supplied) and `home_override=''` (inherit the parent `HOME`) are untouched, exactly as in the existing runners.
- For codex the cleanup runs after the `--output-last-message` file has been read; for hermes after the `config.yaml` written into `HERMES_HOME` has been consumed by the CLI.
- The diff is mostly the re-indent under `try:`; reviewing with whitespace changes hidden shows the actual change (`import shutil`, the `owns_home_dir` line, `try:` / `finally:`).

## Tests

`tests/agent/external/test_runner_home_cleanup.py` (fake environment, no CLI needed), parametrized over the three runners:

- temporary HOME is removed after a successful run
- temporary HOME is removed when the CLI exits non-zero
- a user-supplied `home_override` directory is kept

On `main` the first two cases fail for all three runners (6 failed, 3 passed); with this change 9 passed. `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on the changed files; `test_deepseek_harness_runner.py`, `test_opencode_runner.py`, `test_runner_skill_install.py`, `test_codex_runner.py`: 13 passed, 6 skipped (e2e opt-ins).

title: fix(ifbench): count keywords and person names on word boundaries
body:
## Summary

Two IFBench keyword/name checkers match **substrings** instead of whole words, so they diverge from the official IFBench reference and inflate scores on the `ifbench` benchmark:

- `KeywordsMultipleChecker` (`count:keywords_multiple`) uses `value.lower().count(keyword.lower())`. A required keyword like `art` is counted inside `start`, `smart`, `apart`, so the expected `(1, 2, 3, 5, 7)` occurrence counts are wrong whenever a keyword happens to be a substring of another word.
- `PersonNameCountChecker` (`count:person_names`) uses `if name in value`. Listed names match inside longer words — `Mia` inside `Miami`, `Ava` inside `Available`, `Leo` inside `Leonardo`, `Nora` inside `Norah` — so unrelated text is counted as person names.

Both produce false-positive scores on the official IFBench dataset.

## Fix

Match whole words with a word-boundary regex (`\b...\b`) in both checkers, which is exactly what the upstream IFBench reference implementation does (its `count:keywords_multiple` even carries the comment *"Use regex instead of str.count to avoid counting substrings"*). `re` is already imported in the module.

Bump IFBench `evaluation_version` from `v1.1` to `v1.2` so cached scores cannot silently cross the scoring-semantics change, consistent with the mechanism introduced in #1676.

## Why this matters (real impact)

These checkers run on the standard `ifbench` benchmark. For example:

- keyword `art`, response `"...the art of a start and a smart display..."` → naive `str.count("art") == 4`, so the checker fails a response that actually contains the whole word `art` once.
- name requirement of 1, response `"I flew to Miami last week."` → `"Mia" in value` is `True`, so a response mentioning no person at all is scored as satisfying the instruction.

Both are pure logic bugs, reproducible without any model server, and both currently disagree with the official IFBench scoring.

## Tests

```
pytest -q tests/benchmark/test_ifbench_instructions.py   # 16 passed
ruff check evalscope/benchmarks/ifbench/instructions.py evalscope/benchmarks/ifbench/ifbench_adapter.py tests/benchmark/test_ifbench_instructions.py   # All checks passed
ruff format --check evalscope/benchmarks/ifbench/instructions.py evalscope/benchmarks/ifbench/ifbench_adapter.py   # already formatted
```

Added regression tests for both checkers (substring inputs must now be rejected, whole-word inputs still accepted). Confirmed the new tests fail on the pre-fix code.

title: fix(metrics): parse Chinese multi-select answers separated by 、 or /
body:
### Problem

`parse_answers_zh` drops all but the first label when a Chinese multi-select answer separates its labels with an ideographic comma (`、`) or a slash (`/`).

The English parser (`parse_answers`) already treats both as separators — this is covered by `test_parse_answers_multiple_correct_slash_and_ideographic_comma`. The Chinese path never gained the same handling: its plain-label pattern `_PLAIN_LABEL_ZH_RE` stops at `、`/`/`, and the multi-select branch only normalizes `，` to `,`. So a valid answer is truncated to a single label and scored as wrong.

### Reproduction

```python
from evalscope.utils.multi_choices import parse_answers, parse_answers_zh
# state has choices A/B/C/D, multiple_correct=True

parse_answers(state_en('ANSWER: A、C'),  multiple_correct=True)  # {'A', 'C'}  (English, correct)
parse_answers_zh(state_zh('答案：A、C'), multiple_correct=True)   # {'A'}       <- bug
parse_answers_zh(state_zh('答案：A/C'),  multiple_correct=True)   # {'A'}       <- bug
```

The bracketed form (`答案：（A，C）`) already works because it goes through `_BRACKETED_LABEL_RE`; only the plain/unbracketed form is affected.

### Fix

Bring the Chinese plain-label path to parity with the English one:

- `_PLAIN_LABEL_ZH_RE` now accepts `、` and `/` so the capture is not truncated at the first separator.
- The `multiple_correct` branch normalizes `、` and `/` to `,` before splitting (mirroring `parse_answers`).

Single-answer behavior is unchanged and stays consistent with the English parser (a stray multi-label answer like `答案：A、B` yields no answer in single-select mode, exactly as `ANSWER: A、B` does).

### Verification

```
$ pytest tests/test_multi_choices.py -q
25 passed
```

Added `test_parse_answers_zh_multiple_correct_slash_and_ideographic_comma`, mirroring the existing English separator test. Ran `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on the changed files — both clean.

title: refactor(benchmarks): load adapters on demand instead of importing all 238 at package import
body:
## Problem

`import evalscope` executed **every one of the 238 `*_adapter.py` modules**. Because Python always runs a parent package's `__init__` first, *any* import paid the full cost:

| | before |
|---|---|
| `evalscope --help` (prints 542 bytes) | **16.3 s** |
| `import evalscope.api.registry` (just wants a registry) | **~10 s** |
| modules loaded by `import evalscope` | **3885** |

Adapter module bodies transitively pull `datasets` (4.4 s), `nltk`/`rouge_score` (3.7 s), `openai` (3.4 s) and `pandas`. Every CLI subcommand, the web service, every library-style import and every pytest process paid it. This also contradicted the codebase's own practice — `default_data_adapter.py` and `config.py` already defer imports specifically to keep module load cheap.

## Change

Split **discovery** (which benchmarks exist) from **loading** (executing the adapter module). `evalscope/benchmarks/_index.json` maps benchmark name → adapter module; a new `LazyRegistry` resolves a name by importing only that module.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `evalscope --help` | 16.3 s | **4.2 s** |
| modules after `import evalscope` | 3885 | **1664** |
| resolving one benchmark | — | 0.06 s, +28 modules |

## Behaviour is preserved, not traded away

- **Batch consumers still see the whole catalog.** `keys()` / `values()` / `items()` / iteration / `len()` load everything — that's what `evalscope benchmark-info --list`, the docs pipeline and several tests rely on. `--list` output is **byte-identical** to before (261 lines).
- **A stale index costs time, not correctness.** A name the index doesn't know falls back to a full load and still resolves. There's a test for exactly this.
- **Registration never triggers resolution.** `register_benchmark` uses a write-path membership check, so importing a custom adapter module directly does not drag in the catalog.
- **Unknown names raise the same `ValueError`**, including the `Did you mean:` suggestions.

## `_index.json` is generated, never hand-edited

`evalscope benchmark-info --update-index` writes it, and `make docs-update` / `docs-update-stats` / `docs-pipeline` now run that step. `tests/api/test_benchmark_registry_contract.py` fails if the committed copy drifts from the registry.

**Scope of that guard:** it is a local/pytest check. CI runs a fixed set of test node IDs (`test_ci_lite`, `test_benchmarks`, the perf sweep, and two frontend files) and does not collect `tests/api/`, so a drifted index will not turn CI red. That is deliberate here: because an unindexed name falls back to a full load, a stale index degrades startup time and never changes results.

Why an index at all instead of deriving the name from the path: **44 of 257 names don't match their module leaf** (`aime24`/`aime25`/`aime26` ← `aime.aime_adapter`, `gpqa_diamond` ← `gpqa.gpqa_adapter`, `chinese_simpleqa` ← `chinese_simple_qa.csimple_qa_adapter`) and **11 modules register several names**. A naming convention cannot express that, so the mapping is read from the registry.

## Adjacent defects this surfaced

- `from evalscope.benchmarks import *` published `os`, `glob`, `time`, `importlib` and loop temporaries (`file_path`, `start_time`, …) as public `evalscope` attributes — `evalscope.os` really was the stdlib `os` module — plus a 238-entry `import_times` list nothing ever read.
- `from evalscope.evaluator import *` **rebound `evalscope.evaluator`** to the inner `evalscope.evaluator.evaluator` module, so `evalscope.evaluator.batch_reviewer` / `.execution_tracker` / `.perf_collector` raised `AttributeError`. Now an explicit import; the four public classes stay exported.
- `metrics/nlp/bert_score/utils.py` imported the **root package** for `__version__`, which only worked because a sibling deferred its import. A probe confirms the module-level form raises `ImportError: cannot import name '__version__' from partially initialized module`.
- `utils/data_utils.py` depended on api + metrics + report from inside the leaf `utils` package → moved to `report/data_frames.py`. Two function-local imports of it were redundant (the same module was already imported at module scope in the same file) and one only guarded a cycle that ran through `evalscope.utils`, which the move removes.

## `.importlinter`

Records the resulting import directions. **`core layers must not import benchmark adapters` passes with zero exemptions** — that is the check that detects eager loading creeping back. The other four contracts carry an explicit, reviewable list of the dependencies that exist today; they are a debt inventory, not an excuse list. Type-checking-only imports are excluded, because most of this package's apparent cycles are type-only and treating them as real produces false positives.

**Not wired into CI.** `lint.yml` runs only `pre-commit`, and the pre-commit config has no import-linter hook, so this is a local check via `make lint-imports`. It documents and detects direction regressions for whoever runs it; it does not block a merge. Wiring it into `lint.yml` was considered and deliberately left out of this PR.

## Verification

- **1490 passed** across `tests/api tests/report tests/service tests/evaluator tests/utils tests/metrics`.
- **5 failures, all pre-existing** — reproduced identically on the base commit `9beb3268`: 3 arena-hard judge tests, 1 evaluation-version assertion, and 1 service test that needs `mcp<2` (the env has mcp 2.x).
- `lint-imports`: **5 kept / 0 broken**. `ruff check` and `ruff format` pass.
- `evalscope benchmark-info --list` diffed byte-for-byte against the base commit.
- `tests/cli/test_all.py::TestRun::test_ci_lite` was not runnable locally (needs model/network access); **CI `unit-tests` ran it and passed** (15m14s). All four checks are green: `unit-tests`, `perf-tests`, `run-pre-commit`, `frontend`.

Timings were measured on an NFS-backed checkout, so absolute values are inflated; the before/after comparisons were taken under identical conditions.

title: feat(perf): add real multi-image MMMU dataset mode
body:
Closes #1726.

## What

Adds a discoverable, real-data multi-image mode for `evalscope perf`: a new `mmmu_multi_image` dataset plugin that builds multi-image stress requests from the open-source MMMU validation set, plus EN/ZH user docs for multi-image stress testing.

## Why this instead of existing paths

- The perf transport (`create_message`) already supports multiple `image_url` parts in one message, and `line_by_line` already accepts OpenAI-style messages arrays / full request bodies, so private or constructed multi-image payloads keep working there unchanged.
- What was missing (issue #1726) is a built-in, non-random, open-source multi-image dataset mode plus documentation of the custom-data path. This PR fills exactly that gap without duplicating the generic transport path.

## How it works

- `evalscope/perf/plugin/datasets/mmmu_multi_image.py` (registered as `mmmu_multi_image`): loads MMMU `validation` for the configured `subset` (default `Music`), collects non-empty `image_1` … `image_7` fields in source order (PIL / `bytes`-dict / `path`-dict representations), keeps rows with at least `min_images` images, and yields one user message per row via the shared `create_message(text, image_urls=[...])` path.
- `MMMUMultiImageDatasetArgs`: `subset: str = 'Music'`, `min_images: int = 2` validated to 2–7 (MMMU rows carry at most 7 images).
- `--tokenize-prompt` is rejected with a clear error: multimodal messages cannot be represented as a flat token-ID list.
- Docs: new `docs/{en,zh}/user_guides/stress_test/multi_image.md` (MMMU mode + `line_by_line` custom-data recipe), linked from both stress-test indexes.
- This is stress/performance traffic support, not MMMU benchmark scoring — use `evalscope eval --datasets mmmu` for official scoring.

```bash
evalscope perf \
  --model your-vl-model \
  --url http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  --dataset mmmu_multi_image \
  --dataset-args '{"subset":"Music","min_images":2}' \
  --parallel 4 \
  --number 100
```

## Validation performed

- `pytest tests/perf/test_mmmu_multi_image.py -q` → 4 passed (message structure/order, min-image filtering, arg validation, tokenize-mode rejection; hub loading mocked, no network).
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (repo-pinned ruff 0.16.4) on the touched Python files → clean.

title: fix(evaluator): preserve multi-alias targets for inclusion-based scoring
body:
## Bug

`TaskState.target` always returns `Target.text`, which joins every accepted answer alternative into a single string with **no separator**:

```python
@property
def text(self) -> str:
    return ''.join(self.target)
```

For a benchmark like `trivia_qa`, whose samples set `target` to a list of answer aliases (`record['answer']['aliases'] + record['answer']['normalized_aliases']`), this collapses e.g. `["Oprah Winfrey", "Oprah", "Winfrey, Oprah Gail", ...]` into one unmatchable blob: `"Oprah WinfreyOprahWinfrey, Oprah Gail..."`.

`Accuracy(allow_inclusion=True)` (used by `trivia_qa` and `mmlu_redux`) is explicitly written to accept either a single string or a list of alternatives:

```python
alternatives = [reference] if isinstance(reference, str) else reference
```

but every call site passes `task_state.target`, which is always a `str` - so `alternatives` is always `[the_joined_blob]`, and a correct prediction can never exact-match it. Every sample in `trivia_qa` scores 0 regardless of whether the model's answer was right, because there's nothing left to match against.

Confirmed on a real run: the model answered "Of which African country is Niamey the capital?" with `ANSWER: Niger` (correct), and the sample still scored 0 - the gold reference used for grading was the fully-concatenated alias blob shown above.

## Fix

Return the full list of alternatives from `TaskState.target` when a sample has more than one, instead of always flattening to `Target.text`. Single-target samples (the common case across the rest of the benchmark suite) are unaffected and still return a plain string, since `len(self._target) > 1` is false for them - so this is scoped to exactly the multi-alias case that was broken.

Checked every other call site that reads `task_state.target` for a `str`-only assumption (e.g. `json.loads(task_state.target)` in `researchrubrics`) - none of them ever set a multi-item target, so they're untouched by this change.

title: fix(perf): forward AgentX benchmark grace period
body:
EvalScope's AgentX scenario does not expose the benchmark grace period, so users cannot configure how long to wait for outstanding responses after the sending duration ends. A longer per-request timeout does not extend this separate wait.

Add an optional `benchmark_grace_period` scenario field and forward it to AIPerf's existing `--benchmark-grace-period` option. The value sets the maximum wait after sending stops; it does not require waiting for the entire period when all in-flight requests have completed.

- Omitting the field preserves the existing default (30 seconds with the pinned AIPerf 0.12.0 dependency).
- Finite, nonnegative values are accepted, including zero.
- The sending duration and per-request timeout remain independently configured.
- English and Chinese documentation describe the setting and provide an example.

For example, allow up to 600 seconds for outstanding responses after the 1800-second sending period:

```bash
evalscope perf \
  --scenario '{"name":"agentx","benchmark_grace_period":600}' \
  --duration 1800 \
  --model YOUR_MODEL \
  --tokenizer-path YOUR_TOKENIZER_PATH_OR_ID \
  --url http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  --parallel 1
```

Validation:

- AgentX unit tests: 30 passed, covering smoke and benchmark forwarding, zero, omitted values, invalid values, and independent request timeout/duration.
- `make lint`: passed.
- `pytest tests/cli/test_all.py::TestRun::test_ci_lite -v -s -p no:warnings`: passed using the mock model.

title: fix(agent): stop waiting on a sandbox that never returns
body:
## Problem

Fixes the hang reported in #1685.

`EnclaveAgentEnvironment.exec` hands the deadline to ms_enclave's `shell_executor` and then awaits it with nothing bounding the wait:

```python
result = await handle.execute_tool(
    'shell_executor',
    {'command': shell_argv, 'timeout': timeout_s},
)
```

If the sandbox layer never answers — an unkillable command, a wedged exec channel, a lost reply — that `await` never returns. The sample blocks its worker for the rest of the run, with no traceback and no progress.

`LocalAgentEnvironment` does not have this problem: it wraps the subprocess in `asyncio.wait_for` and returns `timed_out=True` on expiry. Only the enclave path trusts the layer below it to honour the timeout it was handed.

In #1685 the model ran `sphinx-quickstart` inside the sandbox — an interactive CLI whose log tail is `* Please enter some text.` repeated forever, i.e. a prompt loop that never terminates on its own.

### Reproduction

No Docker, no ms_enclave, just a stubbed handle:

```python
class HangingHandle:
    sandbox_id = 'stub'
    async def execute_tool(self, name, args):
        await asyncio.sleep(3600)      # the sandbox never answers

env = EnclaveAgentEnvironment.__new__(EnclaveAgentEnvironment)
env._handle = HangingHandle(); env._timeout = 60.0; env._interpreter = ['bash', '-c']
await asyncio.wait_for(env.exec(['/bin/bash', '-c', 'sphinx-quickstart'], timeout=1.0), timeout=5)
```

```
STILL RUNNING after 5.0s despite exec(timeout=1.0)
```

## Change

`exec` stops waiting at `timeout + _TIMEOUT_GRACE_S` (30s) and returns a timed-out `ExecResult` carrying an explanatory `stderr`. The bash tool renders it as `[TIMEOUT]`, the model sees a failed command, and the run moves on.

The grace is waited out on purpose rather than cutting at the command deadline: ms_enclave reports `TIMEOUT` **together with whatever the command printed before its own deadline**, and that output is the more useful answer. The backstop only decides how long to wait for it before giving up.

## Scope

This bounds the damage. It does not explain why a sandbox would fail to enforce the timeout it was given — that still needs the reporter's `instance_id` and `pip show ms-enclave`, which I asked for on the issue.

Two related gaps I found while reading this code are **not** in this PR, both noted on #1685:

- `exec` accepts `input=` and never uses it, so stdin is silently dropped in a sandbox. `runners/mock.py` passes it; `runners/codex.py` already carries a comment working around it.
- `LocalAgentEnvironment` runs with `stdin=None`, so a child inherits the parent's stdin. Under a pty an interactive command blocks on it for the whole tool timeout (verified locally). `DEVNULL` would make those fail fast.

Happy to send either separately.

## Testing

```
tests/agent/test_t2_environment.py   3 new cases, 57 passed, 10 skipped
  - a handle that never returns is abandoned near the grace window rather
    than hanging (fails on main)
  - a sandbox reporting its own TIMEOUT slightly late is still waited for,
    so its partial output survives
  - a legitimately long command gets timeout + grace, not the grace alone

                                     test_strategy_parsers: optional deps)

title: feat(perf): add optional PD handoff metrics
body:
## Summary

  This PR adds optional metrics for analyzing PD-disaggregated inference serving in `evalscope perf`.

  In PD-disaggregated serving, the first generated token can be produced by the prefill node, while subsequent tokens are produced by the decode node.
  The interval between the first and second streamed output chunks can therefore reflect the P→D handoff path, but it also includes normal decode
  latency. To make this easier to inspect, this PR adds an opt-in metric group behind `--enable-pd-metrics`.

  New metrics:

  - `Steady ITL (ms)`
    - Excludes the first inter-output chunk interval from each request.
    - Intended to represent post-handoff steady decode inter-token/chunk latency.
    - Reported with avg / p50 / p99 / max and percentile JSON entries.

  - `PD Handoff Latency (ms)`
    - Uses the first inter-output chunk interval as a P-D handoff latency proxy.
    - Reported with avg / p50 / p99 / max and percentile JSON entries.

  - `PD Handoff Overhead (ms)`
    - Estimates extra handoff cost as:
      `max(0, first_inter_output_interval - median(subsequent_inter_output_intervals))`
    - This subtracts the steady decode baseline from the first post-TTFT interval.
    - Reported with avg / p50 / p99 / max and percentile JSON entries.

  The metrics are disabled by default, so standard non-PD perf benchmarks keep the existing TTFT / TPOT / ITL output unchanged.

  ## Validation

  Ran the requested perf command with `--enable-pd-metrics` against a local OpenAI-compatible mock service:

  ```bash
  .venv/bin/evalscope perf \
    --url "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions" \
    --api openai \
    --model "mock-qwen" \
    --dataset random \
    --tokenizer-path "/data2/models/Qwen3-0.6B/" \
    --prefix-length 0 \
    --min-prompt-length 100 \
    --max-prompt-length 100 \
    --min-tokens 512 \
    --max-tokens 512 \
    --extra-args '{"ignore_eos": true}' \
    --parallel 10 \
    --number 20 \
    --connect-timeout 120 \
    --read-timeout 1200 \
    --log-every-n-query 100 \
    --enable-pd-metrics \
    --debug \
    --name "test" \
    --outputs-dir "./evalscope"

  Observed the new metrics in both the benchmarking summary and per-request metrics table:

  - Steady ITL (ms)
  - PD Handoff Latency (ms)
  - PD Handoff Overhead (ms)

title: feat(agent): stall the loop when the model repeats the identical tool call
body:
## Problem

`AgentLoop` budgets two ways of failing to make progress:

| failure | budget |
|---|---|
| turn produces no tool call | `max_nudges` (2) |
| turn breaks the output protocol | `max_parse_error_nudges` (3) |

A model that keeps issuing one *valid* call is neither. Every turn is a well-formed `ACT` turn, and an `ACT` turn resets both counters, so the streak never accumulates and the only remaining exit is `max_steps` — with the same tool executed on every step along the way.

That budget is not small:

| benchmark | `max_steps_default` |
|---|---|
| `swe_bench_*_agentic`, `swe_bench_pro`, `gdpval`, `job_bench` | 250 |
| `mcp_atlas` | 100 |
| `gaia`, `wide_search`, `researchrubrics` | 50 |

A model that starts repeating at step 3 of SWE-bench spends the other 247 on real model calls and real sandbox executions. The trace it leaves is shaped exactly like a sample that genuinely needed every step, so "this task was hard" and "the model got stuck immediately" are indistinguishable without reading the turns by hand.

## Change

`NativeAgentConfig.max_repeated_tool_calls`, **default `None` (off)**. It counts consecutive turns whose tool calls match the previous turn's by name *and* arguments. On reaching the threshold the turn is converted into a malformed one: the tools are not executed, the model is told what it keeps repeating, and a model that never changes course ends on the existing malformed-nudge budget.

Measured on a stuck model with `max_steps=250`:

| threshold | model calls | tool executions | terminal reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| `None` | 250 | 250 | `max_steps_exceeded` |
| `3` | 6 | 2 | `parse_error_exhausted` |
| `5` | 8 | 4 | `parse_error_exhausted` |

Nothing changes unless the threshold is set.

## Judgement calls, happy to change any of them

- **In the loop, not in a strategy.** `FunctionCallingStrategy.max_tool_calls_per_turn` is the closest precedent and is strategy-level, but it is a per-turn rule while this one spans turns. Putting the guard in the loop covers all four strategies at once — including `swe_bench_toolcall`, which drives the 250-step benchmarks and would otherwise need its own copy.
- **Reuses the malformed-turn budget** rather than adding a third counter. Both mean "recoverable turn that made no progress", and separate counters would let either failure consume the other's retries — the reason `nudge_count` and `parse_error_nudge_count` were split in the first place.
- **The streak lives on `AgentContext`,** next to those two counters and owned by the loop for the same reason given in their docstrings. It cannot be derived from `ctx.messages`: `swe_bench_backticks` synthesises its `bash` call while parsing a fenced block, so its assistant messages carry no `tool_calls` to compare.
- **Arguments are part of the signature.** A poll that advances an offset, or a retry that changes a parameter, reads as progress. Call *order within* a turn is not part of it, so `{A, B}` and `{B, A}` count as the same turn.
- **`TraceSources.REPEATED_TOOL_CALLS`** marks the `ERROR` event so the guard is distinguishable from a genuine parse error without matching message text. `_emit_parse_error` gained a `source` parameter defaulting to the existing `'parse'`; no existing payload changes.
- **Thresholds below 2 are rejected** by a validator — `1` would stall the first call of every kind.

## Testing

```
tests/agent/test_repeated_tool_calls.py   16 passed
  streak semantics — identical calls trip at the threshold; changed arguments,
                     changed tool name and an idle turn each reset it; order
                     within a turn is irrelevant
  loop behaviour   — the guarded turn does not reach the handler, the model is
                     told and recovers, a model that never changes ends on the
                     nudge budget rather than max_steps, off by default,
                     genuine parse errors keep source='parse'
  plumbing         — the threshold reaches the loop from run_agent_loop,
                     run_native_agent and AgentLoopAdapter, and defaults to None

tests/agent                              357 passed, 21 skipped, same 7 pre-existing
                                         failures (test_sandbox_service,
                                         test_strategy_parsers: optional deps)
tests/cli/test_all.py::TestRun::test_ci_lite   passed
ruff 0.16.4 check + format --diff        clean
```

## Follow-up, not in this PR

The `ERROR` event this emits is a natural input for a trace-derived "degenerate loop rate" alongside tool-error rate and nudge counts, which today are recorded per sample but never aggregated into the report. Happy to open an issue for that separately if it sounds useful.

title: fix(arena): validate review identities before pairing
body:
GeneralArena pairs saved reviews by row position. If candidate indices are `[0, 2]` and baseline indices are `[0, 1, 2]`, it can compare the candidate's answer to question 2 with the baseline's answer to question 1, then silently discard the remaining row. Native saved transcripts also contain generated responses, which must be excluded from the judge's question.

This change validates imported observations before constructing battles. Each shared dataset/subset must have matching, non-empty index sets, consistent supplied sample/repeat identities, and matching inputs. Errors identify the model, dataset/subset, and conflicting indices. Repeated generations retain their individual indices. Duplicate cache rows follow the existing resume convention: use the last saved row and log a warning.

For modern caches, input comparison preserves message roles and structured content while excluding per-run message IDs/metrics. Tool-call IDs are renamed consistently across declarations and references, preserving call/result relationships, function arguments, and provider payloads. Both comparison and the judge's question use only the input prefix before the first generated message; answers remain in their respective answer fields. Explicit legacy `input` rows retain rendered-text compatibility, and unmarked histories remain input because their generation boundary cannot be recovered. The arena evaluation version advances to `v1.2`, and both user guides document the import requirements and recovery steps.

Validation:

- `make lint` — passed.
- `pytest tests/benchmark/test_arena_review_pairing.py tests/benchmark/test_arena_bootstrap.py tests/evaluator/test_cache_manager.py tests/api/test_evaluation_versioning.py tests/api/judge -q` — 198 passed, including 48 native report/JSONL pairing cases.
- Four regression checks fail on the prior PR head: two expose generated content in the question, and two expose false mismatches from tool-call IDs. All pass after the fixes; negative controls still reject changed call/result links, arguments, and provider payloads.
- `pytest tests/cli/test_all.py::TestRun::test_ci_lite -v -s -p no:warnings` — passed with mock model inference.

title: fix(agent): forward exec stdin into the sandbox instead of dropping it
body:
## Problem

`EnclaveAgentEnvironment.exec` accepts `input=` and never reads it — the only occurrence of the name in the file is the signature:

```python
async def exec(
    self,
    cmd: List[str],
    *,
    cwd: Optional[str] = None,
    input: Optional[str] = None,  # noqa: A002 - mirrors ABC signature
    ...
```

`input` is part of the `AgentEnvironment` contract and `LocalAgentEnvironment` honours it, so a caller that pipes a payload gets it in one environment and silently loses it in the other.

- `runners/mock.py` passes `input=task.instruction` and would run against empty stdin in a sandbox.
- `runners/codex.py` carries a comment routing around the gap: *"EnclaveAgentEnvironment (whose `exec` does not forward `input=` to the underlying shell executor)"*.

The base class documents the policy for the analogous case — a subclass that cannot honour `env` *"should raise `NotImplementedError` rather than silently dropping the request"*. Neither branch was taken for `input`.

Found while investigating #1685; unrelated to the hang itself.

## Change

ms_enclave's `shell_executor` takes a command and no stdin, so the payload is piped in by the shell that already runs the rendered command:

```
printf %s <quoted payload> | ( <command> )
```

The subshell is load-bearing. The renderer prepends env exports and a `cd`, so without it a rendered `cd /w && cat` would feed `cd` rather than `cat`:

```
printf %s payload | ( export FOO=bar; cd /w && cat )
```

Supplying stdin this way is shell syntax, so a non-shell `interpreter` now raises `NotImplementedError` rather than dropping the payload a second time.

The two `codex.py` comments describing the gap are dropped since it no longer holds. The positional prompt stays as it is — it keeps the invocation visible in run logs.

## Testing

Verified in a real bash across every shape the renderer produces — bare command, cwd prefix, env prefix, pipelines, and payloads containing newlines, quotes, backticks, `$` and `%`.

```
tests/agent/test_t2_environment.py   5 cases, 4 of them fail on main
  input is rendered as a pipe
  the pipe survives cwd and env prefixes
  the rendered command runs in a real bash and round-trips a payload with
    newlines and shell metacharacters
  no input leaves the command unchanged
  a non-shell interpreter raises instead of dropping the payload

tests/agent   346 passed, 21 skipped, same 7 pre-existing failures
              (test_sandbox_service, test_strategy_parsers: optional deps)
ruff 0.16.4 check + format --diff   clean
```

I don't have ms_enclave installed, so the sandbox side is covered by asserting the exact command string handed to `shell_executor` plus executing that same string in a real shell. If there is a reason `shell_executor` would reject a pipeline, say so and I'll switch to raising `NotImplementedError` instead.

First-stage AgentX integration as proposed in the issue: a dedicated Perf scenario that wraps a pinned/isolated AIPerf executable instead of reimplementing the session-tree scheduler in EvalScope.

## What's included

```
evalscope/perf/agentx/
├── __init__.py
├── config.py   # AgentxArguments + fail-fast validation
├── runner.py   # command construction, executable resolution, version probe
└── result.py   # normalized AgentxResult with provenance + validity
tests/perf/test_agentx.py  # 12 unit tests, no AIPerf install needed
```

**Config** — `--agentx-variant full|256k` maps to the pinned AIPerf public-dataset aliases (`semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126` / `..._256k`); plus tokenizer, random seed, max-context-length, smoke-entry cap, aiperf path, and an `--agentx-extra-args` escape hatch. Scheduler flags that conflict with the scenario locks (`--fixed-schedule`, `--request-rate`, `--ignore-trace-delays`) are rejected up front.

**Runner** — builds the `aiperf profile --scenario inferencex-agentx-mvp` command with the documented scenario-locked flags written out explicitly; strips the endpoint path from `--url` (AIPerf appends it from `--endpoint-type chat`). Executable resolution: explicit path → `aiperf` on PATH → `uvx aiperf`; AIPerf is **not** added to the Perf dependency set. Version is probed and recorded for provenance.

**Result** — parses both export layouts (per-run `profile_export_aiperf.json` top-level metrics; aggregate `aggregate/profile_export_aiperf_aggregate.json` nested `metrics`), preferring the aggregate. Surfaces `submission_valid` + `submission_invalid_reasons`, and adds a `canonical` flag: smoke runs (`--agentx-num-dataset-entries`) are marked non-canonical with an explicit reason, since AIPerf itself still stamps them valid. Missing metrics stay `None` — never reported as zero. Raw artifacts are left untouched.

title: fix(utils): narrow check_import exception handling
body:
check_import previously reported any import-time exception as module-not-found, hiding real breakage behind a pip-install hint. The first revision (catching ImportError only) still misclassified two cases, as pointed out in review: a module body deliberately raising ImportError("boom"), and an installed module failing on its own missing internal dependency (ModuleNotFoundError, an ImportError subclass).

This revision splits discovery from execution, as suggested:

- `importlib.util.find_spec()` decides whether the requested module is truly discoverable; only undiscoverable modules enter the missing-module warning/install-hint/raise_error path.
- A `ModuleNotFoundError` from `find_spec()` on a dotted name counts as missing only when the absent module is the requested module itself or one of its parents (name-prefix check); a broken parent failing on its own internal dependency re-raises untouched.
- `importlib.import_module()` runs outside any handler, so every import-time failure of an available module propagates with its original traceback — never rewritten as "<module> not found".

Behavior and messages for genuinely missing modules are unchanged.

Focused tests in `tests/utils/test_import_utils.py` cover: missing module returns False; missing module with `raise_error` raises `ImportError("not found")`; existing module (`os`) and dotted existing module (`os.path`) return True; body-raised `RuntimeError` / `ImportError("boom")` propagate with the original message and no warning; an internal missing dependency propagates as `ModuleNotFoundError` naming the internal dependency (not the requested module) with no warning; dotted missing parent and dotted missing child of an existing package stay on the missing-module path (False + warning + `raise_error`).

Note: the new tests could not run via repository pytest in this sandbox (collection requires the full installed dependency chain, e.g. `datasets`); they were validated with a standalone harness loading the real `import_utils.py` (9/9 scenarios pass, including fail-before confirmation on the ImportError-family cases). title: feat(web): group same-model reports in the report list, display-only
body:
Resolves #1599.

## Context

Our eval workflow runs one model against datasets incrementally — often as separate invocations (different dataset, different day) rather than one big run. The report list ends up with N unrelated rows per model, with no way to see a model's full picture without opening each report individually.

We tried physically merging report directories in #1570; @Yunnglin correctly closed it because merging mutates/deletes source evaluation runs, which conflicts with reports being immutable audit records. This PR is the display-only alternative discussed on #1599.

## What this does

- `GET /api/v1/reports?group_by=model` rolls same-model report-list items into one row each, entirely in memory, over metadata `_build_report_meta` already loads for the flat list. No report is read, written, moved, or merged.
- Each group carries `children`: every constituent report exactly as the flat list describes it, with its own `run_id`, `model_id`, and `primary_metrics`. A group never shows a fabricated combined score.
- If a dataset appears in more than one of the model's reports, there is no silent "winner" — both stay visible under their respective reports when the group is expanded.
- The response is a new `ListReportsGroupedResponse` (`reports: ReportGroup[]`), kept fully separate from the existing `ListReportsResponse` — the flat endpoint's contract is untouched.
- `ReportGroup` reuses the flat row's field names (`timestamp`, `dataset_name`, `num_samples`) where the meaning matches, so the existing sort machinery and `ReportsTable`/`ReportCard` render the expanded children with no group-aware branching. `refs` (`run_id/model_id` per child) feeds the existing multi-report Compare flow directly.
- The report list UI adds a "Group by model" toggle that renders these as expandable rows.

## Test plan

- [x] Backend: `pytest tests/report/test_report_endpoints.py` (15 passed)
- [x] Frontend: `npx tsc -b` clean, `npx vitest run` (463 passed)

title: refactor(metrics): give metric semantics one source per decision
body:
## Why

`evalscope/metrics/semantics` expressed three decisions twice, and the copies disagreed.

The sharpest consequence, reproduced before the fix:

```
# v1 report: {'dataset_name': 'job_bench', 'metrics': [{'name': 'total_score', ...}]}
v1 path  -> judge_score:identity  quality.judge_score.unbounded  QUALITY   | primary = judge_score
v2 path  -> diagnostic.unspecified                              DIAGNOSTIC | source = BENCHMARK_OVERRIDE
```

`BENCHMARK_METRIC_OVERRIDES` marks `job_bench`'s `judge_score` as a diagnostic because it is the raw sum of passed rubric weights, not a comparable score. The v1 read path consulted the read-old manifest *before* that override, so an archived report promoted exactly the value the override exists to reject — and made it the report's headline.

## What changed

**One source per decision**

| Decision | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Resolution priority | `SemanticsResolver.resolve` and `hydrate_report_semantics`, in different orders | `resolve()` only; reading old differs by one optional `legacy_name` argument |
| Primary metric selection | `select_primary_identity` + two layers of `try/except` in the v1 reader; collection reports skipped it | `select_primary` serves all three producers, never raises, reports authoring ambiguity via `authoring_error` |
| Alias knowledge | five separate declarations | `METRIC_ALIASES`, with `AliasScope` encoding each rewrite's obligation |

The alias scopes are deliberately different sets: a `metric_list` rewrite must keep `get_metric()` resolving, which is the constraint the `bertscore` / `bert_score` mismatch broke; a read-old rewrite may reassign an ambiguous name, which a producer rewrite must never do.

**Correctness fixes**

- `Report.score` no longer falls back to `metrics[0]`, which could present a diagnostic such as `no_answer_num` as the run's score. The frontend already read the primary metric strictly (`primaryMetricOf` never guesses), so this aligns the backend with it — no frontend change needed.
- `olmocr_bench` emitted `aggregation='unit_test_pass_rate'`, undeclared in `KNOWN_AGGREGATIONS`, which was already failing the registry alignment gate on main. Its pooled pass rate is a mean weighted by each page's unit-test count (`sum(passed)/sum(total)`), so it is `weighted_mean`; scores are unchanged.
- A stale gdpval test asserted a metadata key (`judge_strategy_note`) that no longer exists and reached `calculate_metrics` through a configuration `validate_judge_strategy` rejects. It now asserts the grading contract the adapter implements.

**Redundancy removed**

- 68 of 189 read-old catalog entries repeated their `METRIC_DEFINITIONS` declaration verbatim, so a display change had to be made in two places. Removed, with a test forbidding re-addition.
- `identity.py` split into `naming.py` (producer path, never infers) and `legacy_identity.py` (read-old path, deliberately infers) — opposite policies that were mixed in one module.

Net `+1224 / -624` across 28 files; three new concepts (`AliasScope`, `Stage`, `PrimarySelection`), each with an existing caller.

## Behaviour changes

Both are corrections, each locked by a test:

1. A v1 `job_bench` report's `total_score` now reads as a diagnostic and no longer becomes the primary metric.
2. `Acc` migrates to `accuracy` instead of the undeclared `acc`. The producer path already did this; the read path did not, because it consulted the alias table only before snake-casing.

## Breaking surface (internal Python API only)

| Removed / renamed | Replacement |
| --- | --- |
| `metrics.semantics.identity` | `metrics.semantics.naming` / `metrics.semantics.legacy_identity` |
| `metrics.semantics.legacy` | `metrics.semantics.aliases` |
| `resolver.select_primary_identity` | `primary.select_primary` |
| `is_known_dynamic_legacy_name` | `is_known_legacy_spelling` |

No `report.json` field changes, so no `contracts:generate` regeneration and no golden-sample edits.

## New gates

- v1/v2 semantic equivalence: every canonical name must mean the same thing however the report was written; the only permitted divergence (`error_rate`) is pinned by name.
- Per-rule `examples` replace a hand-maintained list of benchmark names, so a new legacy rule without pinned cases fails.
- AST scan replaces a regex that could not see an aggregation passed through a variable, plus a new check that a benchmark forwarding `BenchmarkMeta.aggregation` into an `AggScore` declares a known name.

## Known debt, unchanged and recorded

- `api` → `metrics.semantics` reverse dependency (contract layer depending on the data layer) is untouched; a layering gate cannot be added until it is fixed. `meta.py` keeps exactly one import edge, as before.
- Catalog tables remain mutable `Dict`; no production code mutates them.
- `LEGACY_METRIC_MIGRATIONS` could later move to its own module; deferred until `catalog.py` outgrows its current size.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/report tests/api tests/evaluator tests/metrics tests/service tests/collections` — **1317 passed**
- `pytest tests/cli/test_all.py::TestRun::test_ci_lite` — passed
- Frontend: `vitest` 462 passed / 63 files, `tsc --noEmit` clean, contract schema regenerated with no drift
- `_meta` drift: none; `pre-commit`: all hooks pass

title: test(perf): stop asserting log text in workload_trace tests
body:
## Summary

Six cases in `tests/perf/test_workload_trace.py` fail on pytest 9.0.3 — the version in the project's canonical conda env — while passing on 9.1.1. The code under test is fine; the tests were pinned to a pytest implementation detail.

`tests/perf` now runs **251 passed / 0 failed** on both pytest versions, where 9.0.3 gave 6 failed / 251 passed.

## Root cause

`get_logger()` sets `propagate = False`, and `caplog` installs its `LogCaptureHandler` on the **root** logger, so records emitted by evalscope never reach it and `caplog.text` stays empty. Probing both environments:

| env | pytest | handlers on the `evalscope` logger |
| --- | --- | --- |
| conda `eval`, py3.10 | 9.0.3 | `['StreamHandler']` — no capture handler, `caplog` is blind |
| py3.12 | 9.1.1 | `[..., 'LogCaptureHandler', 'LogCaptureHandler']` — also attached to the non-propagating logger |

So whether the assertions pass depends on the pytest version, not on project behaviour.

This was invisible because CI runs exactly two named tests (`test_ci_lite` and `test_multi_parallel_sweep`); nothing under `tests/perf/` except `test_perf_basic.py` is executed. That gap is worth closing separately.

## What changed

**Dropped the four log-text assertions.** Every one of the six cases also asserts the real behaviour, and all of that is kept: the constrained-decoding guard omits `ignore_eos` while still setting `max_tokens`, the mixed case discriminates per request, and out-of-order timestamps get sorted. The dropped assertions pinned wording. The one that looked substantial — `'1 request(s) use constrained decoding'` — feeds nothing but the log line and is already implied by the two per-request assertions beside it.

A `caplog` adapter fixture (attaching `caplog.handler` to the evalscope logger) was implemented and verified to work on both pytest versions, then rejected: ~24 lines of test infrastructure coupling the project's custom logger to pytest internals, in order to protect phrasing.

**`test_non_monotonic_timestamps_sorted` now asserts through the public API.** It reached into `plugin._records`; it now reads the arrival offsets from `build_messages()`, which are monotonic only if the sort happened. Same coverage, no private access.

**Two unrelated shaves in the same file:**

* `TestArrivalSchedule` was three copies of one test body differing only in `speed` and the expected offsets — now one parametrized case, which also makes the scaling relationship readable as a table.
* `test_rejects_non_positive_completion_tokens` drops `-100`: the guard is a single `<= 0` comparison, so `0` (boundary) and `-1` already cover it.

## Verification

* `pytest tests/perf/test_workload_trace.py` — 60 passed on pytest 9.0.3 and on 9.1.1
* `pytest tests/perf` (excluding the files that need a live endpoint) — 251 passed, 0 failed
* `pre-commit` clean
